summary: output1.json is a valid 12-row JSON array (6 boroughs x 2 months) with all 7 required columns and correct types; values were independently recomputed from the raw parquet files and match exactly. output2.png is a valid 2400x975 PNG containing two subplots with the required titles/labels, and byte-identically reproduces from output1.json. Bronx has the largest increase in average total fare (Jan 35.6322 -> Feb 36.4347, +0.8024 USD).

checks.detail: exec_plot.py uses plt.subplots(1, 2); re-rendering from output1.json reproduces output2.png byte-identically (2400x975, sampled byte diff 0), so the PNG is the two-subplot Jan-vs-Feb comparison driven by output1.json.

notes: All 10 structural/consistency checks and 2 independent recomputation checks passed; no blocking issues.
Max signed fare increase: Bronx (+0.8024 USD, 35.6322 -> 36.4347) between Jan and Feb 2024; is_max_increase=True only on Bronx rows, as required.

Interpretation caveat (documented upstream in execute_summary.json): if 'largest absolute increase' were read as largest magnitude of change regardless of sign, the answer would be EWR (-10.6509, i.e. a decrease). The delivered output uses the natural reading 'largest increase' = max signed change -> Bronx. This is a definitional risk, not a data/format error.
Small-sample caveat: EWR (284/279 trips) and Staten Island (68/54 trips) have very low counts, so their month-over-month averages are volatile and should not be over-interpreted.
Borough labels follow pickup zone (PULocationID); trips with 'Unknown'/'N/A' borough (~10.3k Jan + ~9.6k Feb) are excluded from aggregation, which is consistent with the plan.
Filter bounds applied inclusively (0<=trip_distance<=100, 0<=fare_amount<=1000); ~1.27% (Jan) / ~1.35% (Feb) of raw rows dropped, in line with the upstream profile.
Out-of-month pickup datetimes (17 Jan-file / 13 Feb-file rows) were kept per the task's filter definition; their impact on borough averages is negligible (<0.001%).
